business: Almissa Digital: multilingual websites for small tourism businesses, Omiš/Croatia
by_segment: Villa or apartment-house owner wanting direct bookings to avoid Booking.com commission
Taxi, transfer, tour, rafting or boat operator (takes direct bookings by phone/WhatsApp)
Single-apartment host or small trade (only a Facebook page now)
why_not: I'm 65 and my phone already rings from Google Maps when people search 'taxi Omiš' or 'rafting Cetina'. I've never had a website and the guests still find me, so why pay €600 now?

My bookings already come through Facebook, Instagram, Google Maps and WhatsApp, so I don't see what a website adds. €600 plus €15 every month is real money for something I'm not sure brings even one extra transfer.

Six hundred euros up front plus fifteen every month, and nobody can tell me how many direct bookings it brings. My guests already find me on Booking and message me on WhatsApp, so I'd be paying for a nice page that maybe pays back next year, maybe never.

It's November, I'm shut until spring and nothing is coming in, so €600 now plus €15 every month while I'm closed is money going out for nothing. My regulars and the hotels already call me on WhatsApp, and I can't see this paying back the 600 before summer.

The price is fair and the WhatsApp changes sound like exactly what I needed last time, but I've heard 'we'll keep it updated' before and then nobody answered. I'm not handing over €600 to a name I don't know just from an ad.

The price is fair and my old site with last year's prices does embarrass me, but my guests mostly find me on Google Maps and TripAdvisor, and I have never heard of Almissa Digital. I am not handing €600 to a name I saw in passing; my nephew keeps saying he can do it with Wix.

My guests find me on Booking.com, Google Maps and Facebook, and I've never needed a website. Six hundred euros plus a monthly fee for a site I'd hardly touch doesn't feel urgent while the bookings keep coming.

It's November, my apartment is empty until spring and so is my wallet, so €600 now for something that only pays back in summer is not happening. Maybe I'd think about it in February or March before the season starts.
why_yes: My site still shows last year's prices and I am sick of giving Viator and GetYourGuide a fifth of every booking; €600 is what I lose in commission on a handful of transfers. The domain is in my name and there is no long contract, so if it brings me even a few WhatsApp bookings a month it has paid for itself.

Booking.com takes around 15% of every stay, so if this site plus a tidy Google Maps profile brings me even two or three direct bookings a season, the €600 pays for itself. The domain being in my name was my first worry and they already answered it, and November is the right time to get it done before the season.
flip: Seeing a few sites they already built for other konobas or businesses near me and hearing from one of those owners that changes really get done in two days.
